authors: M. Mack, F. Karlewski, H. Hattermann, S. Höckh, F. Jessen, D. Cano, J. Fortágh
title: Measurement of absolute transition frequencies of 87Rb to nS and nD Rydberg states by means of electromagnetically induced transparency
method: two-step EIT ladder spectroscopy (780 nm + 480 nm) in a room-temperature vapor cell; coupling laser locked to a frequency comb / calibrated wavelength meter
uncertainty: 0.8 MHz per line (8 in the last digit, one row 9); fit residuals rms < 0.75 MHz; quantum defects of nS include a hyperfine correction (text Sec. IV)
conversion: Energies from '87Rb 5P3/2 F=3', energy zero: Adding only 384.2281152 THz refers the values to 87Rb 5S1/2 F=2. Upper levels: nS1/2 rows are the F=2 hyperfine level (hfs shift 3.2(3) MHz at n=19, removed only in the quantum-defect fit); nD hfs negligible.

Shifted by 384.2306782 THz to the ground state hyperfine centre of gravity (computed here from the paper's numbers: 384.2281152 THz (5S1/2 F=2 -> 5P3/2 F=3, Sec. II, Ye et al. 1996) + 3/8 x 6.8346 GHz (87Rb ground hfs = Table II E_i(5S1/2 F=1) - E_i(5P3/2 F=3) - 384.2281152 THz); converts the omega_c frequencies into term energies above the 87Rb 5S1/2 centre of gravity).

Rows with {'l': '0', 'F': '2'} are hyperfine components: shifted by -3.2(0.3) MHz x (nu(19) / nu)^3 with nu = n - 3.1312 to the centre of gravity, the uncertainty of the shift added in quadrature (the paper: the nS F=2 lines include the hyperfine shift of 3.2(3) MHz at n = 19 (Sec. IV), scaled with nu^-3 (consistent with the 87Rb nS hyperfine intervals of Li 2003 at n = 28-33)).
caveats: values are transition frequencies from 5P3/2(F=3), not term energies
nS rows refer to the F=2 hyperfine level, not to the fine-structure centre
87Rb, whereas several other Rb datasets are 85Rb
